data.narrative:
Terranova is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $7M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though the narrow peer set at Seed stage limits triangulation depth.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $7M raised proxy, yielding an $18M implied valuation. This reflects typical markup from Seed to Series A in the robotics sector. Peer-median analysis is not applicable: while eleven same-sector peers exist, only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage comparable were identified—below the three-datapoint minimum needed for robust cross-sectional comparison. Broader sector medians risk masking stage-specific capital intensity and time-to-revenue patterns material to Seed robotics ventures.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $20M, with $18M as the median point. This range reflects uncertainty around capital efficiency relative to the named peer set (Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI). Key sensitivities include proof-of-concept maturity, manufacturing scalability roadmap, and technical differentiation versus the crowded robotics automation sector. Further diligence on unit economics and customer concentration would refine the range as stage progression accelerates.
